findings.claim: The plan says `kmctl doctor` prints the exact new apm.yml entry, and the docs test checks the docs name doctor for it. In the upgrade flow it does not. The new CLI hands every command but briefing off to the release apm.lock.yaml pins whenever that differs from its own (pin.py handoff_pin/project_pin read the lock, not apm.yml). So before `apm install` the lock still says v0.12.2 and `kmctl doctor` runs v0.12.2's doctor, which sees a v0.12.2 install and prints no update fix. After `apm install` the install matches and doctor passes, so `_update_fix` (doctor.py:172) never shows either. Docs that send a v0.12 user to doctor for the entry send them to a command that prints nothing. Fix: write the entry (`path: packages/kmctl/apm`, `ref: vX.Y.Z`) straight into the docs and keep doctor only as the final check, or name `KMCTL_PINNED=1 kmctl doctor` if the entry from doctor is wanted. Then change O1's checked-by to match.
doctor cannot print the new apm.yml entry during the move, because the new CLI hands doctor to the v0.12.x release in apm.lock.yaml.

kmctl's README says auditing a folder of docs against the code 'moved to its own package, kmaudit'. Nothing moved: v0.12.2 users had the action's audit mode (audit: docs-vs-code, okf-vs-code, okf-vs-docs), the /audit skill and the kmctl-auditor agent, and all three still ship unchanged. kmaudit is a new, separate package. A v0.12 user who runs mode: audit would read this as having to install kmaudit, and it contradicts the same README's intro (line 12) and /audit entry (line 312).
